summary: A depth-first checkpoint for the rational all-prime assembly in BSD.8 and its missing-prime regression tests in BSD.9. It decomposes exact finite support, positivity, prime-valuation certificates and real-quotient transfer, using the pinned natural factorization and valuation APIs. The actual elliptic endpoint imports BSD.5. CGS/Keller-Yin proof decompositions and certified curve examples remain explicit work; no rank-zero/one full BSD theorem is asserted.

nodes.title: Prime support of a rational number
nodes.statement: For q in Q, Rat.primeSupport(q) is Nat.primeFactors(|q.num|) union Nat.primeFactors(q.den), using the existing reduced numerator and positive denominator. It is a finite set of natural numbers, not a set of arbitrary places. At q=0 its value is empty by the existing zero convention.
proofSteps: Take the union of the two existing finite prime-factor sets. The construction is deterministic and uses the canonical rational numerator and denominator; it makes no choice of a factorization or rational representative.
acceptance: Changing a displayed fraction by a common nonzero factor does not change its rational prime support.

sources.match: Compose the existing natural-number construction; do not reimplement factorization.

api.name: Rat.mem_primeSupport

nodes.title: Membership in rational prime support
nodes.statement: For q nonzero and p natural, p belongs to Rat.primeSupport(q) if and only if p is prime and either p divides |q.num| or p divides q.den.
hypotheses: q is a nonzero rational number.
proofSteps: Unfold the union defining prime support. Apply Nat.mem_primeFactors to each summand. Nonzero q gives nonzero absolute numerator; the canonical denominator is positive. Remove these two nonzero conditions and distribute the shared primality condition.
acceptance: At q=6/35, 5 belongs to the support and 4 does not. The nonzero hypothesis prevents treating every prime as a divisor contributing to the support of zero.

sources.match: Apply the exact membership theorem to both canonical integers.

nodes.title: Zero valuation in the reduced numerator and denominator
nodes.statement: For a prime p and any rational q with v_p(q)=0, both the natural valuation of |q.num| and that of q.den are zero.
proofSteps: Use Rat.num_or_den_zero_padicVal to obtain that at least one of the numerator and denominator valuations is zero.
Unfold padicValRat. Its vanishing equates the two natural valuations after integer coercion. In each branch, substitute the known zero and deduce that the other valuation is zero.
acceptance: The result also holds for q=0 under the library convention. It must not be applied to an unreduced numerator/denominator pair.

sources.match: Reducedness prevents cancellation between two positive numerator and denominator valuations.

nodes.title: Prime valuation and exact support
nodes.statement: For a nonzero rational q and a prime p, v_p(q)=0 if and only if p does not belong to Rat.primeSupport(q).
proofSteps: For the forward implication, apply zero-numerator-denominator. Use dvd_iff_padicValNat_ne_zero, separately for the nonzero absolute numerator and the positive denominator, to exclude both divisibilities. Apply support-membership.

For the reverse implication, support-membership excludes both divisibilities. The same baseline equivalence gives zero for both natural valuations. Subtract them in the definition of padicValRat. Install Fact p.Prime locally when applying the baseline valuation lemma.
acceptance: For q=1/2, the valuation at 2 is -1 and 2 is in the support; negative valuations are not discarded.

sources.match: Both uses retain the nonzero natural-argument hypothesis.
Identifies the two possible supports.

nodes.title: Empty prime support and rational units of absolute value one
nodes.statement: For nonzero q in Q, Rat.primeSupport(q) is empty if and only if q=1 or q=-1.
proofSteps: A union is empty exactly when each of its finite sets is empty. Apply Nat.primeFactors_eq_empty to the absolute numerator and denominator.

Their nonzero properties eliminate the zero alternatives. Thus the absolute numerator and denominator are both one; the canonical rational normal form gives q=1 or q=-1. Conversely, substitute either value in the definition.
acceptance: Both 1 and -1 must occur. The unrestricted implication with q=0 is false.

sources.match: Apply twice, retaining nonzero q to eliminate the zero numerator.

nodes.title: Reconstruction of a positive rational from all prime valuations
nodes.statement: For q in Q with 0<q, q=1 if and only if v_p(q)=0 for every prime natural p.
proofSteps: If q=1, use padicValRat.one at every prime.

Conversely q is nonzero. Every member of primeSupport(q) is prime by support-membership, and zero-iff-outside-support contradicts its membership if all prime valuations vanish. Hence the support is empty.
Apply empty-support-units. Strict positivity eliminates the alternative q=-1.
acceptance: Reject the conclusion for q=0 and q=-1 when positivity is removed. Testing only odd primes leaves q=2 undecided.

sources.match: This is only the rational reconstruction step, not a theorem establishing positivity or rationality of the BSD quotient.
The proof reduces reconstruction to prime-factor uniqueness at one.

nodes.title: Finite certificate of rational prime-valuation vanishing
nodes.statement: Rat.PrimeValuationCertificate(q) consists of a finite set primes of natural numbers, proofs that every member is prime, that Rat.primeSupport(q) is contained in primes, and that v_p(q)=0 for every member p. It stores no equality q=1, no positivity assumption, and no unproved assertion that a partial list covers the support.
proofSteps: Form the structure using the existing finite-set and valuation types and the explicit primeSupport construction. Constructor fields have the stated mathematical content. Extensionality reduces to equality of the finite sets, since the other fields are proofs.
acceptance: An empty list is not evidence of coverage for q=2. Zero and -1 can have such valuation certificates but cannot pass positive reconstruction.

sources.match: The data consist of finite support coverage and checked local valuations; positivity is a separate hypothesis of reconstruction.

nodes.title: Canonical certificate from all prime valuations
nodes.statement: Given a rational q and a proof that v_p(q)=0 for every prime p, construct Rat.PrimeValuationCertificate.ofAllPrimes(q) with finite set exactly Rat.primeSupport(q). No nonzero or sign hypothesis is needed.
hypotheses: All prime valuations of q vanish.
proofSteps: Choose the canonical support as the finite set; support coverage is reflexive.
Its members are prime by Nat.mem_primeFactors, even when the numerator is zero. The supplied all-prime assertion gives every local proof.
acceptance: The chosen set is canonical rather than an unspecified finite witness.

sources.match: Primality of each member is unconditional.
Packages genuine all-prime input, not a new proof of it.

nodes.title: A finite certificate controls every prime
nodes.statement: For any rational q, any Rat.PrimeValuationCertificate(q), and any prime p, v_p(q)=0.
hypotheses: A finite prime-valuation certificate for q is supplied.
proofSteps: If q=0 use padicValRat.zero. Otherwise split on membership of p in the certificate finite set.
Inside the set use localZero. Outside it, covers implies p is outside canonical support. Apply zero-iff-outside-support to nonzero q.
acceptance: The outside-set branch must be justified by covers. The statement also applies at the zero convention without producing equality to one.

sources.match: This theorem proves that exclusion from the actual coverage field, rather than assuming that the displayed finite list is exhaustive.

nodes.title: Positive reconstruction from a finite certificate
nodes.statement: For strictly positive q in Q, a Rat.PrimeValuationCertificate(q) implies q=1.
hypotheses: A finite prime-valuation certificate for q is supplied.
proofSteps: Use certificate-all-primes to get the valuation statement at every prime. Apply positive-rational-reconstruction with the supplied strict positivity.
acceptance: Neither a certificate for -1 nor one for 0 supplies the positivity hypothesis.

sources.match: This supplies the algebraic identity only after the positive rational defect has been identified by its owner.

nodes.title: Certificate from an exceptional-prime set and an outside theorem
nodes.statement: Given q in Q, a finite set S of primes, vanishing of v_p(q) on S, and vanishing at every prime outside S, construct Rat.PrimeValuationCertificate.ofExceptionSet(q,S) with finite set S. Its support coverage is proved, not an extra unverified field.
hypotheses: Every member of S is prime.
v_p(q)=0 for each p in S.
For every prime p outside S, v_p(q)=0.
proofSteps: For q=0 the canonical support is empty, so coverage is immediate.
For q nonzero and p in canonical support, support-membership gives primality. If p were outside S, the outside theorem and zero-iff-outside-support would contradict membership. This proves coverage.
Use the given primality and inside vanishing statements for the remaining fields.
acceptance: The outside theorem has to cover every prime outside S, not just every sufficiently large prime beyond a second unstated exception set.

sources.match: The inside and outside proofs remain distinct inputs; deriving support coverage does not manufacture any missing prime-part theorem.

api.name: Rat.PrimeValuationCertificate.ofExceptionSet
api.statement: Construct the certificate from inside and outside prime-valuation proofs.

api.name: Rat.PrimeValuationCertificate.ofExceptionSet_primes
api.statement: Its finite set equals the supplied S.

tests.name: Rat.PrimeValuationCertificate.ofExceptionSet_test_empty

tests.name: Rat.PrimeValuationCertificate.ofExceptionSet_test_enlarged

tests.name: Rat.PrimeValuationCertificate.ofExceptionSet_test_negative_one

uses.how: Combines the named source-qualified branches with independent exceptional-prime calculations only after their ranges cover all primes.

nodes.title: Transfer of a certified rational quotient to a real identity
nodes.statement: Let A,B be real numbers with B nonzero. If q is a strictly positive rational number, its canonical real image equals A/B, and q has a finite prime-valuation certificate, then A=B.
hypotheses: The real image of q is exactly A/B.
A finite prime-valuation certificate for q is supplied.
proofSteps: Apply certificate-reconstruction to obtain q=1.
Transport this equality through the canonical rational-to-real map. The identified quotient is one. Multiply by nonzero B using field algebra.
acceptance: The theorem does not assert that arbitrary A/B is rational. It also does not identify A or B with elliptic-curve invariants.

sources.match: An exact rational-to-real identification is indispensable; numerical recognition of a quotient is not this hypothesis.

nodes.title: Full leading term under the actual defect certificate
nodes.statement: Let E be an elliptic Weierstrass curve over Q of analytic rank r in {0,1}, with finite whole Sha. Let d_E be the strictly positive rational defect constructed by BSD.5 and identified there with L*(E,1)/A_E, where L*=L^(r)(E,1)/r! and A_E=Omega_E Reg_E #Sha(E/Q) product_l c_l / #E(Q)_tors^2 is strictly positive. A finite prime-valuation certificate for this actual d_E implies L*(E,1)=A_E. Omega_E is the full real period; no second real-component factor is inserted.
hypotheses: The actual analytic and arithmetic invariants and the exact positive rational defect are supplied by BSD.5.
The analytic rank is 0 or 1 and the whole Sha is finite.
A certificate for this particular d_E is supplied.
proofSteps: Obtain the canonical real identification and positivity of the denominator from BSD.5 with the agreed height, full-period, torsion and regulator conventions.
Apply real-identity with A=L*(E,1) and B=A_E. This proves the conditional leading-term identity without changing any hypotheses of a prime-part supplier.
acceptance: An arbitrary rational carrying the same label is not an admissible substitute for d_E. Keep rank equality and whole-Sha finiteness as separate public results.

sources.match: The theorem is conditional on a complete certificate for the actual curve defect; it is not unrestricted rank-zero/one BSD.

nodes.title: A prime defect is invisible at every other prime
nodes.statement: For distinct primes p and ell, the rational number p has valuation zero at ell.
proofSteps: Nat.Prime.dvd_iff_eq implies ell does not divide p, since ell is not one and the primes differ.
Apply padicValNat.eq_zero_of_not_dvd, then padicValRat.of_nat.
acceptance: With p=2 this verifies all odd-prime checks even though the rational defect is not one. With p=3 the same issue affects an omitted triadic check.

sources.match: Different primes cannot divide one another.
Move the divisibility calculation to the rational valuation.

nodes.title: No complete certificate for a prime defect
nodes.statement: For every prime p, Rat.PrimeValuationCertificate(p), where p is cast to Q, is uninhabited.
proofSteps: Suppose a certificate were supplied. The rational p is positive, so certificate-reconstruction would give p=1. Primality gives p>1, a contradiction.
acceptance: Combine with away-from-prime for p=2: all odd-prime checks pass, but no complete certificate exists. The primitive baseline padicValRat.self gives the missing valuation as one.

sources.match: A rational countermodel tests the logical gate; it is not an elliptic curve or a claim about its Sha.

nodes.title: The remaining dyadic equality under all odd-prime equalities
nodes.statement: For strictly positive q in Q, assume v_p(q)=0 for every odd prime p. Then q=1 if and only if v_2(q)=0.
hypotheses: All odd-prime valuations of q vanish.
proofSteps: Use Nat.forall_prime_iff_two_and_odd to combine the supplied odd-prime results with a dyadic equality, or extract that equality from all-prime vanishing.
Apply positive-rational-reconstruction in both directions.
acceptance: For q=2 and q=1/4 the dyadic hypothesis fails although every odd-prime test succeeds. For q=1 both sides hold.

sources.match: Instantiate the existing prime split with vanishing of the rational valuation.
